meta.title: NUMBER ONE — POLIJE × KNU, Jember 2026
meta.description: Team NUMBER ONE, Kyungpook National University Team 01 of the 2026 World Friends Korea (WFK) IT Volunteer Corps. PlantMoji — a smart-farm learning game built and deployed by nine students from Korea and Indonesia over 22 days in Jember, Indonesia.
hero.eyebrow: 2026 World Friends Korea (WFK) IT Volunteer Corps · Kyungpook National University Team 01
hero.lede: Twenty-two days in Jember, Indonesia, in the summer of 2026. Five students from Politeknik Negeri Jember (POLIJE) and four from Kyungpook National University (KNU) were one team from start to finish. Farming wisdom has always travelled from person to person — we built PlantMoji to carry it on data, all the way to the next generation.
summary.title: 2026 World Friends Korea (WFK) IT Volunteer Corps · Kyungpook National University Team 01, NUMBER ONE
summary.lead: Team NUMBER ONE, Kyungpook National University Team 01 of the 2026 World Friends Korea (WFK) IT Volunteer Corps, won first place in the IT Project category among the nine KNU cohort teams (judged by POLIJE) with PlantMoji, a smart-farm learning kit the team built together with five students from its host institution in Jember, Indonesia, Politeknik Negeri Jember (POLIJE). PlantMoji began with a problem raised by the Indonesian team members — farming knowledge failing to pass from one generation to the next — and is a demand-driven IT project that records growing decisions once left to farmers' experience as sensor data and teaches them through a game. Over 22 days, from 27 July to 17 August 2026, the team taught a smart-farm class to 44 students at SMK Negeri 4 Jember, a local vocational high school, took first place at the K-I Food Day cultural exchange, and took part in every IT education, performance and cultural exchange programme of the KNU cohort, reaching 4,440 local beneficiaries. The team handed its sensor kit over to POLIJE and left the source code in public repositories under both universities' names; its work was featured on KBS 1TV's Docu ON and on the Indonesian local broadcasters KJTV and FTV Jember.

philos.title: From experience to data, from data to the next generation
philos.lede: Farming in Jember still runs on intuition. That intuition is wisdom built over generations. We set out to carry it forward on technology, to the next generation.
philos.s1.title: Experience
philos.s1.body: When to water, what the soil wants — a farmer in Jember knows it by hand. Decades of experience. But only 22% of farmers are millennials, and unrecorded instinct leaves with its generation.
philos.s2.title: Data
philos.s2.body: The sensor writes down, in numbers, what the farmer's instinct already knew. Soil moisture, temperature, humidity, light, pH — once the things a farmer has always measured by hand become a record, that judgement can reach someone who never stood in the same field.
philos.s3.title: The next generation
philos.s3.body: Even a student who has never farmed can start with joy, through play. Clearing quests, earning XP, filling the collection — and along the way, water, soil and light become second nature.
philos.quote: PlantMoji is here to carry farming wisdom forward — to the next generation.
philos.origin: The project began with a problem our local teammates raised. Our Indonesian teammates told us that in Jember, a farming city, the older generation's farming knowledge was not being passed on to the young. We took that problem to the fields and interviewed a farmer, then briefed POLIJE's IT faculty on the design and built their advice — “put the weight on software rather than hardware” — into it. That is how we turned the experience of knowing when to water just by looking at the soil into sensor data for soil moisture, temperature and humidity, light and pH, and we made it an educational kit rather than farm equipment so it could be used again locally after the programme ended. Nine Korean and Indonesian students split the work across hardware, web, mobile and design, built it together over 66 hours, and left the result in public repositories under both universities' names (POLIJE × KNU).
legacy.title: What stayed after we left
legacy.lede: We wanted what we left behind to keep running after the deployment ended.
legacy.sustain: We handed the sensor kit we built over to our host institution, POLIJE, ready for reuse, and the five POLIJE teammates who built it with us are still in Jember. The web app, the mobile app and the source code are public, so anyone can open them and keep building on them now that the programme is over. Back home, team members from both countries stay in touch through a group chat and Discord. This work connects to three targets of the UN Sustainable Development Goals — 4.4 (youth skills: smart-farm and IoT education for 44 vocational high school students), 17.6 (international cooperation in science and technology: joint development by a single team of nine Korean and Indonesian students and the on-site transfer of its outputs) and 2.4 (sustainable agriculture: a learning kit that shifts judgement based on experience to judgement based on sensor data).
legacy.s3.title: Left in a form that can be picked up
legacy.s3.body: We left code. Three public repositories, migration scripts that can rebuild the database from scratch, and documentation written in English, Indonesian and Korean. Tests are in place so a mistake shows itself at once. A POLIJE student next semester can open the repository and continue from today.
team.title:
One team — under one sky — indivisible,
with wisdom and technology, for the next generation.
team.lede: Nine of us shared four roles: PL steering the schedule, TL raising the system, KL shaping what is taught, ML drawing how the team is seen. Each school held every role, so PL worked paired with PL, and TL with TL. Every one of us was a builder.
team.role.PL.desc: Merged two campuses into one schedule and decided what came first each day. Every call was closed with both sides in the room.
team.role.TL.desc: Designed and built the path the data travels, from sensor to web app to mobile. Most of the 280 commits came from these hands.
team.role.KL.desc: Decided at which reading the plant turns thirsty and what each quest should teach — the role that carried the farmer's wisdom into the rules of the game.
team.role.ML.desc: From Jamkachu's expressions to the shop items, the decks and the Instagram — everything the team shows the world.
shipped.title: What we shipped
shipped.lede: The five things we built and shipped. The web app and the mobile app are open right now.
shipped.web.name: PlantMoji web app
shipped.web.tagline: Sensor readings become a mood, and the mood becomes a quest.
shipped.web.body: Sensor readings become the plant's mood, and the mood issues a care quest. Water the plant for real and the next reading confirms it — XP, bond levels and badges follow. Jinseok Seo laid down the architecture and led the build from backend to app, with Yunseong Oh building alongside. The mascot's name, Jamkachu, comes from Jember.
shipped.mobile.name: PlantMoji mobile app
shipped.mobile.tagline: Shipped as a mobile app, too.
shipped.mobile.body: Dashboard, garden, camera, collection, grow diary — five Flutter screens stay in sync with the PlantMoji server. Water the plant on the web, and the Jamkachu on mobile grows with it. The camera scan trims its own upload size so it holds up even on slow local networks. Mobile was led by Dhede and Reno.
shipped.mobile.note: The web app and the mobile app share one game state. Care for the plant from either one and the same progress carries over.
shipped.design.name: Pixel farm design & UI/UX
shipped.design.tagline: Hand-drawn screens became the product itself.
shipped.design.body: Reno's pixel-farm layout became the web app's home screen as drawn — the handover document records it as the "immutable visual source of truth." Kiki filled the world with 300 sprites spanning Jamkachu's growth stages and moods plus six NPCs, and Suhyun Park designed the 31 shop items and Jamkachu's speech bubbles, polishing every screen until it felt right to use.
shipped.design.note: Two cultures sit side by side in the shop — a taegeuk ribbon and a mugunghwa next to a batik pot, a JFC headdress, and a Jember tobacco barn. The colours and pixel feel of this page come from that same design system.
shipped.camera.name: Camera AI
shipped.camera.tagline: An image classifier that runs inside the browser.
shipped.camera.body: An image-classification AI runs inside the browser itself — no server — watching the camera view and judging the growing environment. It is designed to hold back when it is not confident, and the video never leaves the device.
shipped.nodered.name: PlantMoji decision engine
shipped.nodered.tagline: So the plant survives a dropped sensor and a forgetful owner.
shipped.nodered.body: This is where sensor readings become the plant's feelings. It keeps the expression from flickering when a value wavers at the boundary, counts no points while the data is gone, and notices the moment a sensor falls silent.
shipped.nodered.note: Jamkachu wears six expressions — happy, thirsty, overheated, sleepy, and two warnings for soil turning acidic or alkaline.
codev.title: Proof that we built it together
codev.lede: This collaboration is written into the commit log. Who changed whose code, and when — you can verify it right now in three public repositories.
codev.org.label: Where the repositories live
codev.org.desc: Both institutions are written into the organisation name. All three repositories are public.
codev.dir1.label: Main-PlantMoji
codev.dir1.desc: Reno put the Camera AI model he retrained in the field straight into the web app codebase. The background-music system was also built by Reno.
codev.dir2.label: Mobile-PlantEmoji
codev.dir2.desc: Our teammate Jinseok Seo wired the Flutter app to the PlantMoji APIs and made bond level and sensor state actually show up.
codev.shared.label: One shared state
codev.shared.desc: The mobile app's /api/* calls go to the same server as the web app. Both screens see the same level, XP and streak.
retrain.eyebrow: The scene that explains this team
retrain.title: We retrained it in the field
retrain.lede: The model we built misjudged a real greenhouse. Before coming home, we trained it again on site.
retrain.step1.title: First training
retrain.step1.body: We trained and exported the image classifier on location in Jember.
retrain.step2.title: Wrong in the real greenhouse
retrain.step2.body: The growing environment did not look like the scene we had trained on, and the model would not call a safe environment safe.
retrain.step3.title: Retrained and redeployed
retrain.step3.body: We trained it again on site and shipped it into the product. The backbone stayed; only the classifier changed.
retrain.viz.title: What actually changed
retrain.viz.caption: Of 263 weight tensors, 3 changed — all of them in the classifier head. The 410,208 backbone parameters were left alone; only the part that makes the judgement was taught again.

philos.roots: POLIJE is a school with its own line of agricultural IT research — Smart Green House, Agribot SIP. Within that current toward smart farming, we built PlantMoji together, in a form any classroom can touch.
wins.title: First place twice, out of nine teams
wins.lede: Nine teams from the KNU cohort competed under the same conditions. NUMBER ONE took first place in two categories — the IT Project category and the K-I Food Day cultural exchange. The rankings were set by POLIJE faculty and local participants. At the closing ceremony, we also received a plaque of appreciation and a project excellence award.
wins.w1.title: IT Project category
wins.w1.body: We demonstrated the full pipeline live, from sensor kit to web app, and were judged on the system working right there. The kit's hardware was led by Marquez and Rama.
wins.w2.title: K-I Food Day
wins.w2.judge: Participant vote + faculty scoring + Reels likes
wins.w2.body: A booth where we made and shared hwachae and es buah with the participants. It took first place in an evaluation combining participant votes, faculty scoring and the response on Reels.
wins.w3.title: Featured on KBS 1TV Docu ON
wins.w3.body: Team NUMBER ONE's field activities were featured in KBS 1TV Docu ON episode 374, “Jember, Our Summer Vacation.”
wins.w4.title: On Indonesian local TV
wins.w4.body: KJTV's local news programme “KABAR JEMBER” interviewed NUMBER ONE at the final award ceremony on 14 August and brought the project, its expected benefits for the community and the two countries' student collaboration to viewers across Jember. FTV Jember covered the partnership between the two universities at the opening ceremony on 3 August.
ground.smk.title: SMK Negeri 4 Jember
ground.smk.body: The scheduled programme was a K-performance only. We proposed a PlantMoji session, and after discussion with the school it was added to the official schedule. We taught the class together: a Korean team member explained in English, and the Indonesian team leader carried it on in Indonesian. Jimi Lee prepared the session's teaching and presentation materials, and for an hour the 44 students cared for Jamkachu themselves and worked with live sensor data.
ground.smk.note: It was the day PlantMoji first reached the next generation's hands.
ground.smk.stat1.label: became more interested in smart farming
ground.smk.stat2.label: found game-based learning fun
ground.smk.stat3.label: want to grow plants together with classmates in class
ground.smk.survey: In a survey after the class, 18 of the 19 students who responded (95%) said their interest in smart farming had grown, and 18 (95%) said game-based learning was fun. All 19 said they want to grow plants together with their classmates in the classroom. To bridge the gap between how long a plant takes to grow and how short a class is, two days before the class we built an additional “experience mode” that let students go through a plant's entire growth cycle within a single lesson.
legacy.s4.title: Still running
legacy.s4.body: Three services are still on after the deployment ended. The collection and the grow diary hold the records built up in Jember, and the address works the moment you open it. The buttons at the top of this page are that address.
footer.slogan: One Team. One Vision. Infinite Impact.

legacy.s1.title: People who can build it stayed
legacy.s1.body: Nine of us built PlantMoji together, and five are still in Jember. Over three weeks of building side by side, the five POLIJE members got hands-on with Arduino, Node-RED and web and mobile development. They raised this system from the first line, so they can fix it — and grow it.
legacy.s2.title: The same repositories, after the flight home
legacy.s2.body: Working in the same repositories became a habit. With an ocean in between, the code still lands in one place, and we can see each other's commits today.
legacy.snaps.title: Moments saved in the grow diary
legacy.snaps.body: These were taken with PlantMoji's camera in Jember and saved into the grow diary. The students gathered in front of the lens, and the strawberry planted in the kit — they are all in there. Open the diary today and they still are.
